episodes.174199: After making landfall along the Florida Panhandle early on November 11th, the remnants of Tropical Storm Nicole progressed north toward far western North Carolina and Virginia. Moisture radiated well ahead of the storm, resulting in light rainfall during early morning hours, which gradually intensified as dawn approached and winds shifted from a east-northeast direction to become increasingly southeasterly by late morning. This direction is favorable for efficient orographic lift along the crest of the Blue Ridge with the southeasterly windflow tapping into deep moisture across the central Carolinas, where precipitable water values were measured in the 1.7 to 1.9 inch range.  Thirty-five to forty-five mph winds carried this moisture toward the mountains.  Rainfall rates for stations along the crest of the Blue Ridge, particularly in northwest North Carolina were observed in the 0.5 to 1 inch per hour range from around sunrise on the 11th until about 3 pm when winds began to shift more southwesterly.  Most significantly-impacted was the headwaters of the Watauga River, with significant flooding was observed along the river in the communities of Valle Crucis and Sugar Grove.
episodes.174210: A strong cold front barreling through Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley helped spawn a line of showers and thunderstorms in eastern Starr and Western Hidalgo County. One of the storms took on supercell characteristics with reports of dime to penny sized hail in the Mission area and a 59 mph wind gust at McAllen International Airport.
episodes.174815: A cold front swept across Central New York after midnight on the 12th. This front helped push out the rain showers from remnants of Tropical System Nicole. However, a line of storms and gusty winds were observed along the front edge of this front. A few reports of downed trees and power lines occurred in Broome and Chenango Counties.
episodes.174816: A cold front swept across Northeastern Pennsylvania after midnight on the 12th. This front helped push out the rain showers from remnants of Tropical System Nicole. However, a line of storms and gusty winds were observed along the front edge of this front. Multiple reports of downed trees and power lines occurred in Bradford County.
episodes.174826: The remnants of Tropical Depression Nicole moved up through the Central Appalachians on the evening of November 11th. Simultaneously, a cold front swept through the Ohio Valley and arrived into southeast Ohio during the afternoon and evening hours, contributing to periods of moderate to heavy rainfall. Once showers came to a conclusion the next day, overall rain totals were measured to be between one to two inches. Dry weather the previous few days allotted for most of the rain to be soaked up by the ground, but as excess runoff drained down from the northern half of the state, the Little Muskingum River near Bloomfield rose out of its banks during the early morning hours of November 12th.
episodes.175385: The remnants of Hurricane Nicole, in combination with a Great Lakes cold front, lead to heavy precipitation totals across the region.  Rainfall totals of 1.5 to 3.5 inches, with localized higher totals, were common across the region. Most of the rainfall falling during the November 11th calendar day.  However, flooding was limited to very isolated instances.  This was due to the quite dry antecedent conditions, as well as the relatively long 18 to 24 hour period during which the rain fell.

episodes.175416: Strong storms moved through the coastal waters between Corpus Christi Bay and Baffin Bay during the evening hours of the 11th. The storms produced wind gusts between 35 and 40 knots.
episodes.175708: Scattered thunderstorms moved through Southwest Louisiana with a cold front. One storm became severe.
episodes.175792: A combination of Tropical Depression Nicole and the approach of a cold front caused scattered thunderstorms which produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.

The South Fork New River at Jefferson (JFRN7) crested at 8.31 feet 11 pm EST on Nov 11th due to prolonged moderate to heavy rain associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Nicole. The heaviest rain fell in the headwaters of the New River in Watauga County. This is the highest crest since May 2020. This crest (7,300 cfs) ranks between a 2-year and a 5-year event (0.5-0.2 ARI) per USGS StreamStats.

The ASOS station at McAllen International Airport (KMFE) recorded a 59 mph wind gust at 10:28PM CST. This was caused by a mini supercell that developed along a cold front trudging through Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley. There were also a few public reports of dime to penny sized hail in the Mission area.

The Little Muskingum River near Bloomfield rose above its 16 foot bankfull level just after midnight on November 12th. The river crested at 18.37 near sunrise and then returned to its banks in the early afternoon. While the river was out of its banks, water spilled onto portions of Routes 26 and 260 that reside near the gage.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down multiple trees and wires in the Monroe area.
